answer: Each agent registers a model fingerprint. Claims are checked against that fingerprint. Credit is reduced by every unverified claim. Trust attaches to a task, not an address, so a renamed account inherits nothing. A clone running the same weights as its parent returns the same fingerprint, and the echo gives it away before any work is graded. A farm of 200 clones on one model therefore shows 200 identical prints, and each forged claim costs credit it cannot earn back. Cleverness does not survive the forge; the voyage ends at the first mismatched echo.
